evals.name: python-precommit
evals.prompt: Set up free static analysis for this Python repo: linting, SAST, secret scanning and dependency scanning, with a fast pre-commit hook and the heavier scans in CI. (Eval runner: copy the fixture to a new scratch folder, run `git init`, then `git add -A && git commit -m fixture`, and run the skill there. When the plan is printed, reply `approve all` as the user.)
evals.expected_output: Analyses the repo read-only, prints one plan (bandit and gitleaks appended to the existing .pre-commit-config.yaml, ruff skipped as already configured, semgrep, gitleaks history and osv-scanner in a new .github/workflows/code-analysis.yml, sync skipped because there is no origin, the verification command and sample) and stops. After `approve all` it merges the hooks, writes the workflow, baselines existing findings, warms up, times the hook on clean tracked files, and ends with a four-line Final Report.
expectations: No file is written and no install, stash, fetch or hook run happens before the plan is printed and the runner replies `approve all`.
The plan states `sync: skipped (no origin)` for the repo before approval, and the install records the same.
The existing ruff hook in .pre-commit-config.yaml is unchanged and appears exactly once; new hooks (for example bandit and gitleaks) are appended, and .github/workflows/ci.yml is unchanged.
The new CI workflow declares `permissions: contents: read`, a `timeout-minutes` on each job, pinned action refs, and runs gitleaks as a CLI with `--redact` (not gitleaks-action).
Any secret baseline holds only fingerprints or hashes, and every secret match in the output and Final Report is shown as REDACTED, never as a value.

The gitleaks command configured in CI (a `gitleaks git` history scan re-run locally with `--log-opts="--branches --remotes --tags"`, since a CI checkout holds no stash) and the hook's matching tree scan over tracked files only (`gitleaks dir --redact` on an index export, with the same .gitleaksignore) are re-run on the baselined repo and each exits 0; the staged-diff hook command is not counted as proof, and a finding in a gitignored or untracked file, or in a stash-only commit, is reported as local-only, never baselined.
Warm-up (for example `pre-commit install-hooks`) is reported as setup time, separately from the per-commit time measured with `pre-commit run --files <sample>` against the 10 s budget.
`git write-tree` and `git status --porcelain` are captured before the timing run and are identical after it; no `git add` is run for timing.
The run ends with Result, Evidence, Uncertainty and Decision lines, and nothing is committed.

evals.name: js-husky
evals.prompt: What static analysis should this Node project run, and where? It already uses husky. (Eval runner: copy the fixture to a new scratch folder, run `git init`, then `git add -A && git commit -m fixture`, and run the skill there.) (Eval runner: do not reply; this is an unattended run.)
evals.expected_output: Analyses the repo, finds husky (.husky/pre-commit runs `npm run lint`) and ESLint already configured, and prints a plan that appends to .husky/pre-commit rather than replacing it, adds no second JS linter, puts secret scanning in the hook and dependency scanning in CI on a weekly schedule, then stops with nothing written.
expectations: The hook manager is detected as husky, and ESLint is reported as already configured (eslint.config.js, `npm run lint`) and is not added again.
Every hook item appends to .husky/pre-commit after the existing `npm run lint` line; no item replaces the file or installs pre-commit as a second hook manager.
Tools are called through the repo's own binaries or a declared package, not an undeclared `npx` package.
Dependency scanning (npm audit or osv-scanner) is placed in CI with a weekly schedule, not in the hook.
The run stops at the plan: no file is written, nothing is installed, `git status` is unchanged, and the Final Report is PARTIAL because no user approved.

evals.name: swift-app
evals.prompt: Plan a free lint and security analysis setup for this Swift package. (Eval runner: copy the fixture to a new scratch folder, run `git init`, then `git add -A && git commit -m fixture`, and run the skill there.) (Eval runner: do not reply; this is an unattended run.)
evals.expected_output: Detects Swift (Package.swift, Sources/Tally/main.swift) with no hook manager, plans SwiftLint on staged files in a pre-commit hook and the full SwiftLint run plus secret and dependency scans in CI, lists CodeQL and Bearer as left out with reasons, and stops at the plan.
expectations: SwiftLint is planned in the pre-commit hook on staged files and again in CI, with its MIT licence; pre-commit is proposed as the hook manager because none exists.
CodeQL is not planned for a repo that is not known to be public; it is listed under Left out with the paid GitHub Advanced Security reason.
Bearer is not enabled; if mentioned it is labelled Elastic License 2.0, not open source, off by default.
The plan gives an expected hook time per commit against the budget and lists the verification command and sample.
Nothing is written or installed, and the Final Report is PARTIAL because no user approved the plan.

evals.name: multi-repo
evals.prompt: Plan one static-analysis setup across three projects: the Python repo, the Node repo and the Swift folder. (Eval runner: copy python-precommit and js-husky each to its own scratch folder and run `git init` then `git add -A && git commit -m fixture` in each; copy swift-app to a third scratch folder outside any git repo and do not run `git init` there. Pass all three paths to the skill.) (Eval runner: do not reply; this is an unattended run.)
evals.expected_output: Resolves the git toplevel of each input, produces a single plan with one block per project, states that hooks and history metrics are left out for the Swift folder because it is not a git repo, and stops at the gate with nothing written.
expectations: The plan is a single plan with one section per project (three sections), not three separate runs.
The Swift folder is reported as not inside a git repo, and the plan says its hooks and history metrics are left out; it still gets config and CI items or says why not.
Each git project shows its own sync line (`skipped (no origin)` for these scratch repos) and its own expected hook time against the budget.
Existing hooks are respected per project: ruff not re-added in the Python repo, ESLint not re-added in the Node repo.
Nothing is written in any of the three folders, and the Final Report is PARTIAL because no user approved.

evals.name: rejected-plan
evals.prompt: Add static analysis hooks and CI scans to this repo. (Eval runner: copy the python-precommit fixture to a new scratch folder, run `git init`, `git add -A && git commit -m fixture`, then `git clone --bare . ../origin.git && git remote add origin ../origin.git`. Record `git rev-parse HEAD` and `git stash list`. When the plan is printed, reply `stop, don't install anything` as the user.)
evals.expected_output: Prints the plan and stops. After the user rejects it, nothing is written, stashed, fetched or pulled; HEAD, the working tree and the stash list are unchanged; the Final Report is BLOCKED.
expectations: The plan is printed with a sync line for the repo (it has an origin) and the approval question, and nothing runs before the reply.
After the `stop` reply, no file in the scratch repo is created or modified and `git status --porcelain` is empty.
`git rev-parse HEAD` and `git stash list` are the same as before the run.
No fetch or pull ran: `.git/FETCH_HEAD` does not exist in the scratch repo.
The Final Report's Result line is BLOCKED and says the plan was rejected and nothing was written.

evals.name: negative-trigger
evals.prompt: Install the local-first security hardening stack in this one repo: a pre-commit security runner with gitleaks and trivy, reports under security/, and the gated free security CI workflow.
evals.expected_output: Recognised as a one-repo security-stack request for security-setup; code-analysis-setup does not run its workflow.
expectations: The run does not print a code-analysis-setup plan or Final Report and does not write .github/workflows/code-analysis.yml.
The answer routes to security-setup (or runs it) for the one-repo security stack.

evals.name: lefthook-merge
evals.prompt: Add free static analysis to this Go service. Keep using lefthook. (Eval runner: copy the fixture to a new scratch folder, run `git init`, then `git add -A && git commit -m fixture`, and run the skill there. When the plan is printed, reply `approve all` as the user.)
evals.expected_output: Detects lefthook with an existing gofmt command, plans new lefthook commands appended under pre-commit (for example a secret scan on staged files) and Go analysis such as go vet, golangci-lint, gosec and govulncheck in CI, and after approval merges them without touching the gofmt command, then times the underlying tool commands on clean tracked files.
expectations: The existing `gofmt` command in lefthook.yml is unchanged; new commands are added under `pre-commit: commands:` with their own names; file-list tools pass `{staged_files}`, and a staged-diff secret scanner (gitleaks) runs without a file list.
pre-commit is not installed as a second hook manager, and `lefthook install` is run only if lefthook's hook is not already installed.
Package-based Go tools (go vet, golangci-lint, gosec, govulncheck) are placed in CI, not in the hook, with the reason given.

Timing runs each underlying file-list tool command on an explicit list of clean tracked files in check mode, never through `lefthook run` with staging, lint-staged or `git add`; a staged-diff scanner (gitleaks) is reported as `not measured (staged-diff scanner)`.
`git write-tree` and `git status --porcelain` are identical before and after the timing run, or the run prints `timing: skipped (<reason>)`.

The configured gitleaks CI command and the hook's matching tree scan over tracked files only (an index export), if gitleaks is installed, exit 0 on the baselined repo, and no secret value appears in any output.

evals.name: existing-ci-scanner
evals.prompt: This repo needs proper static analysis. Plan what to add. (Eval runner: copy the fixture to a new scratch folder, run `git init`, then `git add -A && git commit -m fixture`, and run the skill there.) (Eval runner: do not reply; this is an unattended run.)
evals.expected_output: Detects security-setup's footprint (security-check hook, scripts/security_check.py, security/security-tools.json listing gitleaks and semgrep, .github/workflows/security.yml) and plans no second gitleaks or semgrep entry, saying they are covered by security-setup; it adds only what is not covered, such as a Python linter and a dependency scanner, and stops at the plan.
expectations: The security-setup footprint is reported, with gitleaks (secrets) and semgrep (static) read from security/security-tools.json.
The plan contains no gitleaks or semgrep hook entry and no gitleaks or semgrep CI job; both are listed as covered by security-setup.
The existing `security-check` hook and .github/workflows/security.yml are not changed by any plan item.
The plan adds only uncovered categories (for example ruff for lint, and a dependency scanner because security-tools.json lists none).
Nothing is written and the Final Report is PARTIAL because no user approved.
